tasks.title: CLP/JPY/KWD amounts rendered with the wrong number of decimals
tasks.summary:
Root cause: `money.Amount.Decimal()` hardcoded a 2-decimal rendering (`m/100`, `%02d`), ignoring `Currency.Exponent`. Every API response (amount, fee, refunded/remaining, refund amounts) goes through `Decimal()`, so CLP/JPY (exponent 0) showed "150.00" for 15000 and KWD (exponent 3) showed "12.34" for 1.234. Fee math itself is in minor units and was correct; only its rendering was wrong.

Fix (money/amount.go): `Decimal()` now uses `Currency.Factor()` to split major/minor units, emits no decimal point for exponent-0 currencies, zero-pads the fraction to exactly `Exponent` digits otherwise, keeps the minus sign for negatives, and avoids the `-math.MinInt64` overflow by taking absolute values of quotient and remainder separately. USD/2-decimal output is unchanged. No public API changes.

Tests (money/money_test.go): added `TestDecimalExponents` (CLP, JPY, KWD, negative, zero, MinInt64 cases) and `TestParseDecimalRoundTrip` (Parse→Decimal round-trips for each exponent). `go vet`, `gofmt -l` and `go test -race ./...` are clean.

tasks.title: Multiple partial refunds can exceed the captured amount
tasks.summary:
PAY-4420: Fixed over-refunding in `payment.Service.Refund`. The guard compared the requested refund against the payment's full amount (`amount.Minor > p.Amount.Minor`) instead of the remaining refundable amount, so any refund up to the full amount passed regardless of earlier refunds (1000 → 600 + 600 = 1200 refunded, remaining -200). The check now uses `p.Remaining()`, so a refund larger than what is left is rejected with the existing `ErrRefundExceedsRemaining` (mapped to 422 `refund_exceeds_remaining` by the API), the payment is not modified and no event is published; refunding exactly the remaining amount still succeeds and moves the payment to REFUNDED. Concurrent refunds remain safe via the repository's optimistic locking (loser gets `ErrVersionConflict`/409).

Added regression tests: `TestRefundCannotExceedRemaining` (payment package: ticket scenario, payment untouched after rejection incl. version/updatedAt/events, exact-remaining refund → REFUNDED, further refund → invalid transition) and `TestRefundsCannotExceedPaymentAmount` (api package: HTTP-level 201/422/201 flow with refunded_amount/remaining_amount/status assertions). No public API changes; `go test -race ./...`, `go vet` and `gofmt -l` are all clean.

tasks.title: Cursor pagination silently drops one payment per page
tasks.summary: PAY-4432: Fixed an off-by-one in cursor paging in `store.Memory.ListByMerchant`. The `next_cursor` already encodes `end`, the index of the first item of the next page, but the decode path then did `offset++`, so every page after the first skipped one payment (19 skipped at limit=50 over 1,000 payments → 981; half lost at limit=1). Removed the increment and documented the cursor contract (cursor = offset of the first item of the requested page). The existing `end < len(ids)` check already yields an empty cursor on the last page, including exact multiples of the limit, so no change was needed there. Added regression tests in store/memory_test.go: `TestListWalkAllPages` walks all pages for limits 1, 3, 50, 100, 250, 999, 1000 and 0 (default) and asserts every payment is returned exactly once in creation order with the expected page count and an empty final cursor; `TestListCursorPastEnd` covers a cursor beyond the end. No public API changes; `go test -race ./...`, `go vet ./...` and `gofmt -l .` are all clean.

tasks.title: Webhook dispatcher retries permanent 4xx failures and gives up on 5xx
tasks.summary:
PAY-4450: the webhook dispatcher's `retryable` classifier had its status classes inverted — it treated every 4xx as transient (so 400/401/404/410 were hammered MaxAttempts times with backoff) and never matched 5xx (so a 503 outage dead-lettered after one attempt). This contradicted the retry policy in the README and its own doc comment.

Changes in `webhook/dispatcher.go`:
- `retryable` now returns true only for transport errors, 408, 429 and 5xx; all other non-2xx statuses are permanent and go straight to the dead-letter list.
- `deliver` tracks the number of real sends in a dedicated `attempts` variable (instead of relying on the loop counter's post-loop value) so `DeadLetter.Attempts`/`LastStatus` always reflect what actually happened, and clamps `MaxAttempts` to at least 1 so a misconfigured policy can't produce a phantom dead letter with zero sends. No public API or constructor signatures changed.

Tests added in `webhook/webhook_test.go`: permanent 400/401/404/410 → exactly one POST, no sleeps, dead letter with Attempts=1 and LastStatus set; 503/500 → retried with 1s/2s backoff then delivered; mixed 503/429/408/502 → exhausts MaxAttempts (4) and dead-letters with Attempts=4, LastStatus=502; cancelled context → Flush returns context.Canceled and the event stays queued. `go test -race ./...`, `go vet ./...` and `gofmt -l .` are all clean.

tasks.title: Idempotency keys never expire after 24h
tasks.summary:
PAY-4461: Fixed idempotency TTL in idempotency/store.go. Root causes: (1) Memory.Begin never checked ExpiresAt on a hit, so correctness depended entirely on the lazy purge; (2) the purge evicted only when now - ExpiresAt > ttl, i.e. at 2×TTL (48h) — explaining both the 40h replay and two days of memory growth.

Changes:
- Added `expired(r, now)` helper (`!now.Before(r.ExpiresAt)`, i.e. expired once now >= first use + TTL).
- Begin treats an expired record as absent and starts a fresh request regardless of fingerprint; pre-expiry replay/reuse/in-progress semantics are unchanged.
- purgeLocked evicts at `now >= ExpiresAt` instead of 2×TTL.
- Complete/Release treat an expired record as ErrUnknownKey and drop it, so a stale late completion can't resurrect/clobber an expired key.
- Updated Len doc comment.
- Added regression tests: restart at exactly TTL for completed/same-fp, completed/different-fp and in-progress records; no expiry at TTL-1ns (replay still works, ErrKeyReuse still raised); eviction from memory after TTL and ErrUnknownKey on Complete/Release of expired keys.

No public API or constructor changes. `go test -race ./...`, `go vet ./...` and `gofmt -l .` all clean.

tasks.title: Every client error is returned as 500 internal_error
tasks.summary:
PAY-4475: `api.errorResponse` mapped domain errors to HTTP status/code with `switch err { case payment.ErrNotFound: ... }`, i.e. identity comparison. Since last release every layer wraps errors with `fmt.Errorf("...: %w", err)` (store → service → handler), so no sentinel ever matched and every domain error fell through to 500 `internal_error`.

Fix (api/errors.go): replaced the identity switch with an ordered table of sentinel → (status, code) checked via `errors.Is`, honouring the README convention ("match them with errors.Is"). Mapping is unchanged: not_found 404, invalid_transition 409, conflict 409, refund_exceeds_remaining 422, invalid_request 400 (ErrInvalidInput, ErrInvalidCursor, money.ErrInvalidAmount/ErrPrecision/ErrUnknownCurrency/ErrCurrencyMismatch). Matched errors keep their full contextual message; unknown errors still return a generic 500 "internal error" without leaking details. No public API or constructor changes.

Tests (api/errors_test.go, new): unit tests for `errorResponse` with multiply-wrapped and `errors.Join`ed errors for every sentinel plus the generic-500 path, and an end-to-end HTTP test covering the ticket's scenarios (GET unknown → 404, double capture → 409, over-refund → 422, malformed body → 400, bad precision → 400, refund of unknown payment → 404, bad cursor → 400). `go build`, `go vet`, `gofmt -l` clean; `go test -race ./...` passes.

tasks.title: Late webhook retries fire with no delay
tasks.summary:
PAY-4488: Fixed the webhook retry storm caused by integer overflow in `Policy.Backoff`.

Root cause: `Backoff` computed `BaseDelay << (n-1)` as an unchecked int64 shift. With BaseDelay=1s (~2^30 ns), from attempt ~34 the shift wrapped to zero/negative; those values passed the `d > MaxDelay` check and were returned, so `clock.Sleep` returned immediately and the remaining attempts fired back-to-back (matching the ~18 same-second requests for a 48-attempt policy). The existing test only exercised n ≤ 6 so never hit it.

Fix (webhook/dispatcher.go): rewrote `Backoff` to double the delay iteratively and saturate at MaxDelay as soon as the next doubling would exceed it (loop is bounded to ~63 iterations regardless of n). Result is now always positive, non-decreasing in n, and capped at MaxDelay for any attempt number and any BaseDelay/MaxDelay. Also treats n < 1 as 1, handles MaxDelay <= 0 by saturating at the max duration instead of wrapping, and returns 0 for a non-positive BaseDelay (misconfiguration) rather than spinning. Public API/signature unchanged.

Tests (webhook/webhook_test.go): kept the existing schedule test and added `TestBackoffLargeAttemptsNeverOverflow` (invariants over several policies incl. the enterprise one, up to n=300 and a huge n) and `TestDeliverEnterprisePolicyAlwaysWaits` (end-to-end: 48 failing attempts produce 47 positive, non-decreasing sleeps capped at 1h). `go test -race ./...`, `go vet ./...` and `gofmt -l .` all pass.

tasks.title: Add payment cancellation (CANCELED status + endpoint + webhook)
tasks.summary:
PAY-4502: added payment cancellation before capture.

Domain (payment/payment.go, payment/service.go):
- New `StatusCanceled` ("CANCELED") added to the status constants and `allStatuses`, so `ParseStatus` accepts it case-insensitively; `Status.Final()` now returns true for it.
- New `(*Service).Cancel(ctx, id)` built on the existing `mutate` helper (optimistic locking + event publish). Allowed from CREATED and PENDING; otherwise wraps `ErrInvalidTransition`; unknown ids surface the repository's wrapped `ErrNotFound`. Emits "payment.canceled", which flows through the webhook dispatcher like every other event. Because Authorize/Capture/Decline/Refund already reject any status outside their explicit allow-lists, a canceled payment is automatically rejected by them (409) with no further changes.

HTTP (api/handlers.go, api/server.go):
- New route `POST /payments/{id}/cancel` -> `cancelPayment`, reusing `respondPayment` so it returns 200 with the payment body, and the existing error mapping yields 409 invalid_transition / 404 not_found.

Tests & docs:
- payment: `TestParseStatus` extended with "canceled"; new `TestCancel` covers CREATED→CANCELED, PENDING→CANCELED, unknown id, non-cancelable statuses, event emission, finality and that all operations are rejected after cancel.
- api: new `TestCancelPayment` covers 200 body, webhook enqueued, 409 for every follow-up op (incl. refunds), 404 for unknown id, 409 for a succeeded payment.
- README lifecycle diagram and event list updated.

Public constructors and existing APIs are unchanged; go vet, gofmt and `go test -race ./...` all pass.

tasks.title: Filter the merchant payment listing by status
tasks.summary:
PAY-4510: added an optional status filter to the payments listing endpoint.

- `payment.Page` gained an optional `Status` field (zero value = no filter), so the `Repository` interface, constructors and all existing callers are unchanged.
- `store.Memory.ListByMerchant` now filters by status while scanning the merchant's creation-ordered ids. The cursor remains an offset into that list, positioned just after the last returned item, so pages are filled to `limit`, items keep creation order and each match is returned exactly once. It looks ahead for a further match so `next_cursor` is empty after the last one. Unfiltered behaviour is identical to before.
- `payment.Service.List` validates/normalises `page.Status` via `ParseStatus` (wrapping `ErrInvalidInput`).
- `api.listPayments` parses the `status` query parameter case-insensitively with `payment.ParseStatus`; unknown values map to `400 invalid_request` through the existing error mapping.
- Added tests: store-level filtered pagination walk (full pages, exact-boundary page, no matches, bogus status) and an API test walking `next_cursor` with `status=succeeded` plus the 400 case. README documents the parameter.
- `go vet`, `gofmt -l` and `go test -race ./...` all pass.

tasks.title: Replay a dead-lettered webhook event
tasks.summary:
Implemented PAY-4523 (replay of dead-lettered webhooks).

webhook package:
- Added exported `ErrDeadLetterNotFound`.
- Added `func (d *Dispatcher) Replay(ctx, eventID) (delivered bool, err error)`: atomically removes the dead letter by event id (under the mutex), then re-runs the normal `deliver` path with the same `Event` (same id and payload; signature recomputed at send time as usual). Returns (true, nil) on success, (false, nil) if it dead-letters again (the new DeadLetter entry carries the new attempts/status, and the event appears exactly once), and an error wrapping `ErrDeadLetterNotFound` for unknown ids. If ctx is cancelled mid-retry the original dead letter is restored so the event is never lost; if the merchant has no endpoint anymore the event is re-dead-lettered with an explanatory error instead of being silently dropped.
- Refactored `deliver` to return a `deliveryOutcome` (dropped/delivered/dead-lettered) alongside the ctx error; `Flush` behaviour is unchanged.

api package:
- New route `POST /webhooks/dead-letters/{eventID}/replay` → 200 `{"event_id": "...", "delivered": bool}` (`replayResponse` DTO).
- `errorResponse` maps `webhook.ErrDeadLetterNotFound` to 404 `not_found`.

Tests: added webhook tests for replay delivered (same Webhook-Id/body, valid signature), fails again (exactly one dead letter with new attempts/status), unknown id, and ctx cancellation; added an API test covering the endpoint for the not-delivered, delivered and 404 cases. README updated. `go vet`, `gofmt -l .` clean, `go test -race ./...` passes. Public constructors and existing APIs unchanged.

tasks.title: Accept and return integer minor units, backward compatible
tasks.summary:
PAY-4530: Added integer minor-unit amounts to the API, backward compatible.

- api/dto.go: `createPaymentRequest` and `refundRequest` now carry `Amount *string` (legacy decimal) and `AmountMinor *int64` (`amount_minor`); pointers distinguish absent from zero so presence rules can be enforced. `paymentResponse` gains `amount_minor`, `fee_minor`, `refunded_minor`, `remaining_minor`; `refundResponse` gains `amount_minor`. All existing fields are unchanged and `toPaymentResponse` is used by every payment-returning endpoint (get, authorize, capture, decline, refund, create, list), so the new fields appear everywhere.
- api/handlers.go: new `resolveAmount(decimal, minor, currency)` helper used by both create and refund: neither present -> `ErrInvalidInput` (400 invalid_request); only `amount_minor` -> `money.New` (unknown currency still 400); both -> parse decimal and require `Minor` equality, otherwise 400. Non-integer / string `amount_minor` values fail JSON decoding (400), and `DisallowUnknownFields` remains so unknown fields are still rejected. Zero/negative amounts continue to be rejected by the service.
- Idempotency: fingerprints were already computed from the resolved `money.Amount` (minor units), so a retry in the other format with the same value replays the stored response; a different value is still rejected with 422.
- Tests: added coverage in api/api_test.go for create/refund via `amount_minor`, both-present agree/disagree, raw JSON field presence, list responses, validation cases, and cross-format idempotent replay. README updated. `go vet`, `gofmt -l .` and `go test -race ./...` all pass; no public constructors or signatures changed.

tasks.title: Centralize the payment status machine in one transition table
tasks.summary:
PAY-4541: Centralised the payment state machine.

- payment/payment.go: added a `transitions` table (CREATED->PENDING/DECLINED, PENDING->SUCCEEDED/DECLINED, SUCCEEDED->REFUNDED) and the public `CanTransition(from, to Status) bool`, which is now the only place that knows which status changes are legal (no self transitions, unknown statuses never allowed). Added a small unexported `(*Payment).transition(to, op)` helper that consults CanTransition and otherwise returns the same `ErrInvalidTransition`-wrapped error text as before ("cannot <op> a <STATUS> payment").
- payment/service.go: Authorize, Capture, Decline and Refund no longer contain any `switch p.Status`; they go through `transition`/`CanTransition`. Refund gates eligibility with `CanTransition(p.Status, StatusRefunded)` up front, so a partial refund is allowed exactly when a full one would be, and only applies the actual SUCCEEDED->REFUNDED transition when the full amount has been refunded. Validation order, event types, returned payments and wrapped errors (ErrInvalidTransition, money.ErrCurrencyMismatch, ErrRefundExceedsRemaining, ErrInvalidInput) are unchanged.
- payment/service_test.go: added TestCanTransition covering every (from, to) pair including self transitions and unknown statuses.

Public API/constructors unchanged apart from the new CanTransition function. gofmt, go vet and `go test -race ./...` all pass.

tasks.title: Idempotency store is not safe under concurrent retries
tasks.summary:
PAY-4555: Fixed data races and the duplicate-start bug in idempotency.Memory.

Root cause (idempotency/store.go):
- Begin did a check-then-act across two separate lock sections: concurrent retries could both see "no record" and both return started=true (→ duplicate refunds). It also read record fields (Fingerprint/Completed/Response) after unlocking, racing with Complete.
- Complete accessed the map and mutated the record with no lock at all (→ `fatal error: concurrent map read and map write`).
- Release read the map outside the lock before deleting inside it.

Fix: each of Begin/Complete/Release now holds m.mu for its entire duration (lock + defer unlock), so the lookup, purge and reservation in Begin are one atomic critical section. For a given key exactly one concurrent Begin gets started=true; the rest get ErrInProgress or, after Complete, the stored response. Public API, constructor and behaviour of the existing tests are unchanged.

Tests (idempotency/store_test.go): added TestConcurrentBeginStartsExactlyOnce (64 goroutines racing Begin on the same key; asserts exactly 1 started and 63 ErrInProgress) and TestConcurrentMixedOperations (hammers Begin/Complete/Release/Len across goroutines so -race catches any regression). `go test -race -count=3 ./...`, `go vet ./...` and `gofmt -l .` all pass.

tasks.title: In-memory repository shares mutable state with callers
tasks.summary:
Root cause (PAY-4561): store.Memory copied payment.Payment by value but Payment.Refunds is a slice, so Get/ListByMerchant handed out values sharing the stored backing array and Create/Update stored the caller's slice. Two concurrent Refund calls that both loaded version N appended into the same backing array (DATA RACE), and the loser of the optimistic-lock check left its refund entry behind in the stored payment (phantom refund with amounts not matching refunded_amount).

Changes:
- store/memory.go: deep-copy with Payment.Clone() at every boundary — Create and Update store a clone, Get and ListByMerchant return clones. Optimistic locking logic unchanged.
- payment/service.go: mutate() now clones the loaded payment before applying the change, passes a clone to repo.Update, and gives the published Event its own clone, so the service is race-free even with repositories that leak shared state, and the async webhook dispatcher never aliases the value returned to the caller. Public API and constructors unchanged.
- Tests: store/memory_test.go gains TestNoSharedStateAcrossBoundary (mutations after Create/Get/Update/List and a conflicting stale update never affect the stored payment); payment/concurrency_test.go (external package, uses store.Memory) runs 32 concurrent refunds and asserts no phantom refund ids, refunds sum to Refunded, and one version increment per successful update.

Verified with go test -race -count=3 ./..., go vet ./..., and gofmt -l . (all clean).

tasks.title: Idempotency Begin gets slower with every stored key
tasks.summary:
Root cause (PAY-4570): `idempotency.(*Memory).purgeLocked` copied every stored record into a slice and sorted it on *every* `Begin`, making each POST O(n log n) in the number of live idempotency keys — hence p99 growing with traffic until a pod restart emptied the map.

Fix in `idempotency/store.go`:
- Added an `expiryHeap` (container/heap min-heap of `*Record` ordered by `ExpiresAt`). `Begin` pushes the new record (O(log n)); `purgeLocked` now only pops entries from the heap head while they are expired, so its cost is proportional to the number of expired records, amortized O(log n) per record, and independent of the total number of live keys.
- Stale heap entries (from `Release`, or an expired key being re-begun) are detected by pointer identity (`m.records[key] == r`) and skipped, so a live newer record is never evicted by an old entry.
- Full sweeps are throttled to at most once per minute (`purgeInterval`), as permitted by the ticket.
- Expiry semantics are unchanged: the lookup still requires `now.Before(r.ExpiresAt)`, so an expired key is never replayed even before it has been swept, and expired records are still evicted so memory stays bounded. Public API, `Store` interface and `NewMemory` constructor are untouched.

Tests added in `idempotency/expiry_test.go`: expired key not replayed and evicted (boundary now == ExpiresAt), purge evicts only expired records, released/replaced keys don't corrupt purge, a scaling check (Begin with 50k live keys stays well under 1ms/call) and a benchmark. `go vet`, `gofmt -l` and `go test -race ./...` all pass.

tasks.title: Split payouts do not reconcile with the charged amount
tasks.summary:
PAY-4588: Fixed money.Allocate so split payouts always reconcile.

Root cause: each part was computed as float64(a*ratio/total) and rounded independently with math.Round, so rounding errors never cancelled — 100.00/3 paid 99.99, 0.10 in sevenths paid 0.07, and 0.05 in halves paid 0.06 (over-payment).

Fix (money/allocate.go): implemented the documented largest-remainder contract in exact integer arithmetic. Each part gets the floor of its proportional share (using bits.Mul64/Div64 so a*ratio can't overflow, in the same overflow-conscious spirit as Fee), then the leftover minor units are handed out one each to the parts with the largest remainder, ties broken by lower index via a stable sort. Also guarded the ratio sum against int64 overflow with ErrInvalidAmount. Signature and error semantics are unchanged.

Tests (money/money_test.go): added TestAllocateReconciles with the exact ticket scenarios (3334/3333/3333, 2,2,2,1,1,1,1, 3/2) plus tie-breaking, zero ratios, zero amount and single part; and TestAllocateInvariants, which checks the exact-sum and within-one-minor-unit guarantees across many amounts/ratio sets including values near int64 limits. Existing tests untouched; `go test -race ./...`, `go vet ./...` and `gofmt -l .` are all clean.

tasks.title: Identical retries rejected as idempotency key reuse
tasks.summary:
Root cause: `bodyFingerprint` hashed the raw request bytes, so a retry whose JSON was re-encoded by the SDK (different key order/whitespace, `"usd"` vs `"USD"`, `"10.5"` vs `"10.50"`) produced a different fingerprint for the same Idempotency-Key and was rejected with 422 `idempotency_key_reused` — pushing clients into a second manual attempt and duplicate payments.

Fix (api package, no public API changes):
- Replaced `bodyFingerprint` with `requestFingerprint(r, fields...)` + `amountFields(amount)`, which hash the canonical parsed request: URL path, merchant_id, amount in minor units (`int64`) and the normalized ISO currency code. Any encoding of the same semantic request now yields the same fingerprint; a genuinely different request (other amount/currency/merchant) still produces a different one and is rejected.
- `createPayment` and `refundPayment` now compute the fingerprint after decoding/parsing (which they already did before the idempotent op), so no double body reads are needed; removed the now-unused bytes/io/payment imports from idempotency.go.
- Added regression tests `TestIdempotentCreateReplaysReencodedBody` and `TestIdempotentRefundReplaysReencodedBody` using the exact payloads from the ticket, asserting the retry is replayed (`Idempotent-Replayed: true`, identical body), only one payment/refund is created, and a different amount under the same key is still 422.

Verified: go build, go vet, gofmt -l (clean), go test -race ./... all pass; existing tests untouched.

tasks.title: Processing fees overcharged by one cent
tasks.summary:
Root cause (money/fee.go): `Fee` used `math.Ceil` on a float64 product, so (1) every fee with a fractional part was rounded *up* instead of half-to-even as documented on `money.Fee` (10.05 USD @ 290 bps → 0.30 instead of 0.29), and (2) for amounts above 2^53 minor units the float64 multiplication lost precision, producing fees off by several units.

Fix: rewrote `Fee` with exact integer arithmetic. The amount is split as `q*10000 + r` so `q*bps` (≤ a.Minor since bps ≤ 10000) and `r*bps` (< 1e8) can never overflow int64; the exact remainder is then rounded half-to-even (round up if > ½, round up on exactly ½ only when the truncated fee is odd). Signature, error values and validation behaviour are unchanged.

Tests: added `TestFeeRoundsHalfToEven` (ticket example plus tie-to-even cases) and `TestFeeLargeAmountsExact` (2^53+1 and MaxInt64 cases). gofmt, go vet and `go test -race ./...` all pass.
